chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdul Malik ibn Utba al-Hashimi, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) about a man who has dinars for one of his associates, so he takes silver dirhams in their place for his needs. On the day he took possession, the rate was seven and seven and a half dirhams per dinar. The owner of the wealth might seek some of the silver, but it is not present, so he buys it for him from the money-changer at this price or similar. Then the price changes before they account for it, until the silver becomes twelve dirhams per dinar. Is that permissible for him, given that when he took possession, the rate was seven and seven and a half per dinar?
He (peace be upon him) said: When the silver is handed over to him in accordance with the dinars, the fluctuation in exchange rates does not harm him, and there is no problem.
ai.seo_question: Is delayed delivery of silver in a gold-silver exchange valid if the price changes before delivery?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the ruling on deferred delivery in currency exchange (sarf), affirming that the transaction remains valid provided the specific amounts are delivered as agreed, regardless of subsequent market fluctuations. It highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between the validity of the contract based on the agreed terms at the time of exchange and the risk of price variance borne by the holder. This ruling underscores the flexibility in commercial transactions within Islamic jurisprudence, prioritizing the fulfillment of the agreed quantity over fixed monetary value stability.
